knowledge:
- key_parameters: order=The order statistic used in aggrPvals to aggregate multiple p-values (e.g., order=2) ;; fdr=The False Discovery Rate threshold used in scoreNodes to calculate node scores from the BUM model ;; plot=Logical parameter in fitBumModel to control whether the BUM model fit is plotted ;; use.score=Logical parameter in writeHeinzEdges indicating whether to write edge scores to the output file ;; attr=The attribute name (e.g., "geneID") used in mapByVar to map expression probesets to network nodes
- alternatives: runFastHeinz=A heuristic alternative to runHeinz that does not require a commercial CPLEX license ;; jActiveModules=An alternative Cytoscape plugin heuristic mentioned in the text, though BioNet's heuristic is shown to yield a closer approximation to the optimal solution
- when_to_use: Use this package when you want to identify a connected subnetwork (functional module) of genes that are significantly active or differentially expressed across conditions, integrating transcriptomic p-values with a PPI network.
- pitfalls: self_loops=Self-loops must be removed from the network using rmSelfLoops before running Heinz or writing Heinz files ;; cplex_license=The exact runHeinz algorithm requires an external CPLEX license; without it, users must use runFastHeinz ;; multiple_probesets=When multiple probesets map to a single gene, mapByVar should be used to select the probeset with the highest variance to avoid duplicate mapping ;; disconnected_components=The network should be restricted to its largest connected component using largestComp to ensure the identified module is a single connected subgraph

workflows.name: heuristic_module_detection
workflows.intent: Identify active functional modules from aggregated p-values and a PPI network using a fast heuristic approach without requiring CPLEX.
input: pvals_matrix.txt (matrix of p-values for genes across different analyses)
workflows.stages: 1. Aggregate multiple p-values using aggrPvals ;; 2. Extract a subnetwork of the PPI network using subNetwork and remove self-loops with rmSelfLoops ;; 3. Fit a Beta-uniform mixture (BUM) model to the aggregated p-values using fitBumModel ;; 4. Score the nodes of the subnetwork using scoreNodes with a specified FDR ;; 5. Run the fast heuristic module detection using runFastHeinz ;; 6. Plot the resulting module using plotModule
workflows.code:
pvals <- cbind(t=dataLym$t.pval, s=dataLym$s.pval)
rownames(pvals) <- dataLym$label
pval <- aggrPvals(pvals, order=2, plot=FALSE)
subnet <- subNetwork(dataLym$label, interactome)
subnet <- rmSelfLoops(subnet)
fb <- fitBumModel(pval, plot=FALSE)
scores <- scoreNodes(subnet, fb, fdr=0.001)
module <- runFastHeinz(subnet, scores)
logFC <- dataLym$diff
names(logFC) <- dataLym$label
plotModule(module, scores=scores, diff.expr=logFC)

workflows.name: exact_module_detection
workflows.intent: Identify the exact maximum-scoring subnetwork by exporting network files for the external Heinz ILP solver (CPLEX) and reading the results back into R.
input: expression_data.gct (ExpressionSet or matrix of gene expression values)
workflows.stages: 1. Map expression probesets to network nodes using mapByVar ;; 2. Extract the subnetwork using subNetwork, get the largest connected component using largestComp, and remove self-loops using rmSelfLoops ;; 3. Perform differential expression analysis (e.g., using limma) to get p-values ;; 4. Fit a BUM model using fitBumModel and score nodes using scoreNodes ;; 5. Write network edges and node scores to files using writeHeinzEdges and writeHeinzNodes ;; 6. Run the external Heinz solver (outside R or via runHeinz) ;; 7. Read the Heinz output graph back into R using readHeinzGraph ;; 8. Add attributes to the module and save as XGMML using saveNetwork
workflows.code:
mapped.eset <- mapByVar(ALL, network=interactome, attr="geneID")
network <- subNetwork(rownames(mapped.eset), interactome)
network <- largestComp(network)
network <- rmSelfLoops(network)
library(limma)
design <- model.matrix(~ -1+ factor(c(substr(unlist(ALL$BT), 0, 1))))
colnames(design)<- c("B", "T")
contrast.matrix <- makeContrasts(B-T, levels=design)
fit <- lmFit(mapped.eset, design)
fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, contrast.matrix)
fit2 <- eBayes(fit2)
pval <- fit2$p.value[,1]                                
fb <- fitBumModel(pval, plot=FALSE)
scores <- scoreNodes(network=network, fb=fb, fdr=1e-14)
writeHeinzEdges(network=network, file="ALL_edges_001", use.score=FALSE)
writeHeinzNodes(network=network, file="ALL_nodes_001", node.scores = scores)
datadir <- file.path(path.package("BioNet"), "extdata") 
module <- readHeinzGraph(node.file=file.path(datadir, "ALL_nodes_001.txt.0.hnz"), network=network)
nodeDataDefaults(module, attr="diff") <- ""
nodeData(module, n=nodes(module), attr="diff") <- fit2$coefficients[nodes(module),1]
nodeDataDefaults(module, attr="score") <- ""
nodeData(module, n=nodes(module), attr="score") <- scores[nodes(module)]
saveNetwork(module, file="ALL_module", type="XGMML")

workflows.name: consensus_module_detection
workflows.intent: Assess variation and identify robust consensus modules using a jackknife resampling procedure.
input: expression_data.gct (ExpressionSet or matrix of gene expression values)
workflows.stages: 1. Resample microarrays and calculate p-values using resamplingPvalues over multiple replicates ;; 2. Fit BUM models and score nodes for each replicate ;; 3. Write resampled node scores to file ;; 4. Read the resulting modules from the external solver ;; 5. Calculate consensus scores for nodes and edges using consensusScores ;; 6. Write consensus scores to file using writeHeinz and solve ;; 7. Read the consensus module using readHeinzGraph and plot with robust node sizes and edge widths
workflows.code:
j.repl <- 100
resampling.pvals <- list()
for(i in 1:j.repl)
{
  resampling.result <- resamplingPvalues(exprMat=mapped.eset, groups=factor(c(substr(unlist(ALL$BT), 0, 1))), resampleMat=FALSE, alternative="two.sided")
  resampling.pvals[[i]] <- resampling.result$p.values
  print(i)
}
fb <- lapply(resampling.pvals, fitBumModel, plot=FALSE, starts=1)
resampling.scores <- c()
for(i in 1:j.repl)
{
  resampling.scores[[i]] <- scoreNodes(network=network, fb=fb[[i]], fdr=1e-14)
}
score.mat <- as.data.frame(resampling.scores)
colnames(score.mat) <- paste("resample", (1:j.repl), sep="")
writeHeinzEdges(network=network, file="ALL_e_resample", use.score=FALSE)
writeHeinzNodes(network=network, file="ALL_n_resample", node.scores = score.mat)
datadir <- file.path(path.package("BioNet"), "extdata") 
modules <- readHeinzGraph(node.file=file.path(datadir, "ALL_n_resample.txt.0.hnz"), network=network)
cons.scores <- consensusScores(modules, network)
writeHeinz(network=network, file="ALL_cons", node.scores=cons.scores$N.scores, edge.scores=cons.scores$E.scores)
datadir <- file.path(path.package("BioNet"), "extdata") 
cons.module <- readHeinzGraph(node.file=file.path(datadir, "ALL_cons_n.txt.0.hnz"), network=network)
cons.edges <- sortedEdgeList(cons.module)
E.width <- 1+cons.scores$E.freq[cons.edges]*10
N.size <- 1+cons.scores$N.freq[nodes(cons.module)]*10
plotModule(cons.module, edge.width=E.width, vertex.size=N.size, edge.label=cons.scores$E.freq[cons.edges]*100, edge.label.cex=0.6)
